messages:
matt: heads up — saw a sustained saturation event on primary redwood-7b in us-west around 11:02. Standard-tier requests started getting 429/latency spikes. thinking we should enable automatic variant fallback by tier+region (capacity-based). propose: prefer same-region compatible quantized variant (redwood-7b-q4) then cross-region fallback if needed. thoughts?
jess: +1. protect enterprise SLAs first. policy should be: prefer same-region compatible variant, fall back only if latency SLO or slot availability breached. maintain sticky routing where possible (session affinity).
anita: we need both a global default and per-tenant override. API flag example: `X-RW-Fallback: auto;prefer_region=true;tiers=enterprise,standard` so ops can opt certain tenants into more aggressive fallback.
omar: compatibility matters — not all variants support function-calling/structured outputs. router must check model capability matrix before rerouting. otherwise we risk malformed outputs.
matt: agreed — easy solution: router runs a quick `can_handle(schema)` check from metadata catalog. If incompatible, skip variant and try next. always tag telemetry with `fallback_reason`.
jess: telemetry/priorities: emit metrics `fallback_count`, `fallback_reason` (CAPACITY|SLA|REGION|INCOMPAT), `from_variant`, `to_variant`, `tenant_id`, `latency_delta_ms`. Console should have a per-model fallback heatmap and per-tenant 24h fallback diff.
deploy-bot: rollout started: feature/auto-fallback-v2 -> staging :rocket:
anita: console UX: need a toggle in tenant page: "graceful demote" (opt-in). shows warning: "Responses may differ when served by a fallback variant (quantization/accuracy changes)." also show last 7 days fallback count and example diffs.
omar: billing detail: if we serve a cheaper variant, billing should reflect served variant but also surface `requested_variant` vs `served_variant` in usage logs so customers can reconcile. add `X-RW-Served-Variant` response header.
jess: agreed. also include `X-RW-Fallback-Probability` in logs for sampled requests during experiment.
anita: tenant-level policy options: `fallback_policy` = block|queue|fallback. default fallback for standard tier, block for enterprise unless tenant opts in. we should avoid silent behavioral changes.
matt: rollout plan: start with sampling experiment — 1% traffic auto-fallback for standard, 0.1% for enterprise. collect quality_regression scores with eval prompts. if regression > threshold, pause.
sre-bot: alert rule suggestion: `alert if fallback_rate_for_any_enterprise_tenant > 2% over 5m`
jess: implementation sketch for router:```
# pseudocode
if available_slots(primary_variant) < threshold or tail_latency(primary_variant) > SLO:
  for candidate in prefer_list(primary_region, compatibility=True):
    if candidate.has_slots() and candidate.can_handle(request.schema):
      route_to(candidate)
      emit_telemetry(fallback_reason=CAPACITY, from=primary, to=candidate)
      return
  # fallback cascade: cross-region -> smaller model
  route_to(degrade_variant)
```
anita: subtle but important: KV cache keys must be namespaced by variant_id. otherwise a redwood-7b response could be misused by redwood-7b-q4. also warm-up probes for the variant to populate caches after a first route.
omar: we should also add a compatibility matrix version to tenant config so that rollouts can fail fast if a tenant depends on exact behavior. eg `compat_matrix_version: v2`
matt: console rollout UX: on model page show a "Simulate fallback" button that runs 100 sample prompts through candidate fallback chain and shows diffs plus q/regression scores. operators can then toggle per-tenant `fallback_policy`.
jess: good. telemetry dashboard: table with columns [tenant, requested_variant, served_variant, fallback_rate, avg_latency_delta, last_fallback_ts]. also a timeseries for fallback_rate per-region per-tier.
anita: security/compliance: for tenants with strict data residency, block cross-region fallback. router should consult tenant metadata and skip cross-region candidates.
matt: thanks — I'll write an RFC with API header examples, telemetry schema, console mocks, alert rules, and an experimental rollout plan. volunteers to co-author?
jess: I'll take telemetry + dashboard mockups.
anita: I'll do API surface + tenant policy schema.
omar: I'll handle router changes and compatibility matrix updates.
sre-bot: reminder: add runbook entry for investigating spike-driven fallbacks (how to determine if a fallback was helpful vs masking infra fault).
